ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r5.claim: The wording is more fair and gentle than the previous formulation: it calls the believers' deed a crime, as opponents claim, though it earns reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r5.anchor: هذا أدخل في الإنصاف وأبلغ من الأول، وأكثر تلطفا واستدراجا، حيث سمى فعله جرما، كما يزعمون، مع أنه مثاب مشكور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r6.claim: Another possible reading assigns the believers' crime to them rather than the Messenger: they may commit minor sins, while the opponents' deeds are disbelief and major sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r6.anchor: وقد يراد بأجرمنا نسبة ذلك إلى المؤمنين دون الرسول، وذلك ما لا يكاد يخلو المؤمن منه من الصغائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r7.claim: A view cited in the source says this verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p548/r7.anchor: قيل: وهذه الآية منسوخة بآية السيف

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.claim: Two verses on Iblīs lead into challenges that the Prophet is instructed to put to the disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r12.anchor: Two verses regarding the nature of Iblīs (vv. 20–21) then segue into a series of challenges the Prophet Muhammad is told to pose to the disbelievers (vv. 22–30).

STUDYQURAN:34:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:25/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:34:25/r1.claim: Muslims and disbelievers are each responsible for their own religion and deeds, not the religion or deeds of the other.
STUDYQURAN:34:25/r1.anchor: this verse recalls that the Muslims and the disbelievers bear no responsibility for the religion of the other

STUDYQURAN:34:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:25/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:25/r2.claim: The verse also evokes the principle that no person bears another's burden.
STUDYQURAN:34:25/r2.anchor: it evokes the general principle that none shall bear the burden of another

BURSEVI:v7p228/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p228/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p228/r1.claim: Jurmun, with damma, means sin and originally means cutting; al-Mufradat explains that it was extended to acquiring anything disliked.
BURSEVI:v7p228/r1.anchor: والجرم بالضم الذنب وأصله القطع واستعير لكل اكتساب مكروه كما في "المفردات"

BURSEVI:v7p228/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p228/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p228/r2.claim: What the speakers attribute to themselves is the small lapses and slips no believer avoids; the interlocutors' deeds refer to disbelief and major sins, though each person answers for his own work.
BURSEVI:v7p228/r2.anchor: أي : فعلنا واكتسبنا من الصغائر والزلات التي لا يخلو منها مؤمن {ولا نسأل عما تعملون} من الكفر والكبائر

BURSEVI:v7p228/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p228/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p228/r3.claim: This is more fair and less disputatious because the speakers call even a minor lapse a sin in themselves, while describing the opponents' greater crimes neutrally as deeds.
BURSEVI:v7p228/r3.anchor: وهذا أبلغ في الإنصاف وأبعد من الجدل والاعتساف حيث أسند فيه الإجرام وإن أريد به الزلة وترك الأولى

TABATABAI:34:25-27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r1.claim: Each person bears his own deeds, especially evil deeds, and their consequences do not pass to someone else; the two sides answer for their own actions.
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r1.anchor: العمل وخاصة عمل الشر لا يتعدى عن عامله ولا يلحق وباله إلا به

TABATABAI:34:25-27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r2.claim: The Prophet calls his side’s actions crimes but describes the opponents’ actions neutrally as what they do, observing good manners in debate.

TABATABAI:34:25-27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r3.claim: The statement prepares for the next verse: because the sides differ in good and evil actions, they must be gathered and separated so each receives the reward or punishment due to it.
TABATABAI:34:25-27/r3.anchor: وهذا تمهيد لما في الآية التالية من حديث الجمع والفتح

TABRISI:34:25/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:25/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:25/r4.claim: If the unbelievers reject the argument, Muhammad is to say they are not asked about our sins, nor we about their deeds; each person is judged for his own actions.
TABRISI:34:25/r4.anchor: أيها الكفار { عما أجرمنا } أي اقترفنا من المعاصي

TABRISI:34:25/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:25/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:25/r5.claim: The verse shows that no one may be taken to account for another person's sin.
TABRISI:34:25/r5.anchor: بل كل إنسان يسأل عما يعمله ويجازي على فعله دون فعل غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p364/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p364/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p364/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says you will not be called to account for our crimes, and we will not be questioned for your disbelief and rejection; this disavows them and their deeds, like 109:6, and predates the sword.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p364/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا تؤاخذون بجرمنا، ولا نسأل عن كفركم وتكذيبكم، وهذا # على التبري منهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r4.claim: The declaration of separation from their deeds resembles the statement, “You have your religion, and I have mine.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:24-26/r4.anchor: وهذا كقوله تعالى: لكم دينكم ولي دين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r8.claim: The disavowal of responsibility parallels 11:35 and 10:41, where each side bears its own wrongdoing and the other is innocent of it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p759/r8.anchor: كقوله: {قل إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي وأنا بريء مما تجرمون} [هود: 35] .

BURHAN:v2p312/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p312/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p312/r6.claim: This tactful formulation achieves its aim indirectly; the blunt surface wording would instead say that the audience is not questioned about what we did and we are not questioned about their crimes.
BURHAN:v2p312/r6.anchor: فحصل المقصود في قالب التلطف وكان حق الحال من حيث الظاهر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1099/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1099/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1099/r1.claim: In this invitation context, assigning possible wrongdoing to the believers while neutrally saying opponents’ “deeds” is scrupulously fair, meant to win their hearts and keep the door of preaching open.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1099/r1.anchor: هذا من باب الإنصاف في الكلام حتى يستميلهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r1.claim: Saying “what we have done wrong” is exemplary fairness: the Messenger avoids calling the other party a liar, seeking to open hearts and draw them in.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1101/r1.anchor: هذا من باب الإنصاف كما أنت تتكلم مع شخص

ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r1.claim: The disclaimer is maximally fair: believers call their inevitable slips crimes, while opponents' grave disbelief is called mere deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r1.anchor: الأجرام المنسوب إلى النفس بصيغة الماضي الدالة على التحقق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r2.claim: Past tense presents the believers' crimes as established; present tense for opponents' actions does not presuppose them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r2.anchor: الأجرام المنسوب إلى النفس بصيغة الماضي الدالة على التحقق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r3.claim: Some say the verse contains an indirect allusion, which does not compromise the fairness just described.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r3.anchor: وذكر أن في الآية تعريضا وأنه لا يضر بما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r4.claim: Some classify the verse as leaving the dispute and claim the sword verse abrogated it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p141/r4.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنها من باب المتاركة وأنها منسوخة بآية السيف

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r6.claim: If opponents openly claim that they are guided and the Muslims astray, the response is even fairer: neither side demands an account from the other, and each may follow the way that becomes clear.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r6.anchor: أمره أن يجيبهم على هذا التقدير بما هو أبلغ في الإنصاف من الأول

BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r7.claim: The believers say they will not be questioned by their opponents about their own errors, nor question the opponents’ deeds; they leave them and others to follow whichever path is clear.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p178/r7.anchor: فاتركونا والناس غيركم كما أنا نحن تاركوكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r1.claim: The clause is set off so listeners can consider it on its own; it can be an initial resumption while also interrupting the argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r1.anchor: وأيضا فصلت لتكون هذه الجملة مستقلة بنفسها ليخصها السامع بالتأمل في مدلولها فيجوز أن تعتبر استئنافا ابتدائيا ، وهي مع ذلك اعتراض بين أثناء الاحتجاج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r2.claim: Each group bears its own account: ‘being asked’ stands for the reward for good work and the matching recompense for wrongdoing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r2.anchor: فمعنى : { لا تسألون } { ولا نسأل } ، أن كل فريق له خويصته . والسؤال : كناية عن أثره وهو الثواب على العمل الصالح والجزاء على الإجرام بمثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r3.speaker: كعب بن زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r3.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr’s phrase ‘you are questioned’ means held accountable for what came before, illustrating ‘question’ as a figure for reckoning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r3.anchor: كما هو في قول كعب بن زهير : وقيل إنك منسوب ومسؤول أراد ومؤاخذ بما سبق منك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r4.claim: The believers’ ‘we have sinned’ adopts the polytheists’ accusation, as the polytheists taunted believers for rejecting their idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r4.anchor: وإسناد الإجرام إلى جانب المتكلم ومن معه مبني على زعم المخاطبين ، قال تعالى : { وإذا رأوهم قالوا إن هؤلاء لضالون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r5.claim: The past tense ‘we sinned’ treats their alleged guilt as established according to the polytheists’ claim; the present ‘you do’ anticipates their future work and hints they may come to faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r5.anchor: وهذه نكتة صوغه في صيغة الماضي لأنه متحقق على زعم المشركين . وصيغ ما يعمل المشركون في صيغة المضارع لأنهم ينتظرون منهم عملا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r6.claim: This fair, conciliatory formulation leaves the opponents space to reflect instead of being distracted by debate; believers admit alleged guilt and leave their actions broadly stated so reflection can reveal the truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r6.anchor: وهذا ضرب من المشاركة والموادعة ليخلوا بأنفسهم فينظروا في أمرهم ولا يلهيهم جدال المؤمنين عن استعراض ومحاسبة أنفسهم . وفيه زيادة إنصاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r7.claim: This verse does not concern participation in fighting and is not abrogated by the fighting verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r7.anchor: وليس لهذه الآية تعلق بمشاركة القتال فلا تجعل منسوخة بآيات القتال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r8.claim: The repeated ‘say’ renews emphasis so this argument stands independently rather than depending on the preceding one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r8.anchor: إعادة فعل { قل } لما عرفت في الجملة التي قبلها من زيادة الاهتمام بهذه المحاجات لتكون كل مجادلة مستقلة غير معطوفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r9.claim: The sentence explains the previous argument: each group is questioned about its own acts, and God will judge between them truly when He gathers them on the Resurrection Day they deny.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p194/r9.anchor: وأيضا فهي بمنزلة البيان للتي قبلها لأن نفي سؤال كل فريق عن عمل غيره يقتضي أن هنالك سؤالا عن عمل نفسه فبين بأن الذي يسأل الناس عن أعمالهم هو الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r7.claim: The statement that each side answers for its deeds is a truce and disengagement, abrogated by the sword verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r7.anchor: قل لا تسئلون عما أجرمنا الآية مهادنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p419#2/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the truce and the statement about God judging between them are abrogated by the sword verse.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r1.claim: The opponents will not be held to account for the believers' sins, nor the believers for the opponents' disbelief and denial; the wording disavows them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r1.anchor: والمعنى إظهار التبري منهم وهذه الآية عند أكثر المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r2.claim: Most exegetes say this verse was abrogated by the sword verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية عند أكثر المفسرين منسوخة بآية السيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p455/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi rejects the claimed abrogation, saying there is no basis for it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r1.claim: The statement expresses reciprocal disavowal: the groups are separate, inviting one another to God and exclusive worship; acceptance brings fellowship, while rejection leaves each disavowing the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {قل لا تسألون عما أجرمنا ولا نسأل عما تعملون} : معناه التبري منهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir connects this reciprocal disavowal to Jonah's declaration that each side is responsible for its own deeds and to the separation expressed in Surat al-Kafirun.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p517#2/r2.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {وإن (3) كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون}

NASAFI-FULL:v3p327/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p327/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p327/r1.claim: This is more fair-minded: the wording assigns crime to the speakers and action to their audience, pairing censured wrongdoing with praised, commanded deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p327/r1.anchor: هذا أدخل فى الانصاف من الأول حيث أسند الاجرام إلى المخاطبين وهو مزجور عنه محظور والعمل إلى المخاطبين وهو مأمور به مشكور

QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قل لا تسألون عمآ أجرمنا } أي اكتسبنا

QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r2.claim: The speaker seeks the audience's good, not protection from any harm their disbelief might cause him; both sides will be recompensed. The wording resembles “you have your religion and I have mine.”
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r2.anchor: أي إنما أقصد بما أدعوكم إليه الخير لكم، لا أنه ينالني ضرر كفركم

QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r3.claim: Qurtubi calls this a verse of truce and disengagement, abrogated by the sword; another view is that it was revealed before the sword verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:25/r3.anchor: فهذه آية مهادنة ومتاركة، وهي منسوخة بالسيف. وقيل: نزل هذا قبل آية السيف
